Lena (ML): Quick drop-in — ran the shelf-testbed sweep on the new 11.5B candidate (fp16, int8, int4) with our prod prompt set. TL;DR: int8 looks like the best cost/quality tradeoff for now.
Mike R: Can you paste the small scorecard?
Lena (ML): Sure — compact numbers below (avg over 3 runs, 1k prompts):
Lena (ML): ```
- fp16: latency p50 210ms, p95 480ms, cost per 1k tokens $1.12, quality delta +0.0
- int8: latency p50 185ms, p95 420ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.58, quality delta -0.9
- int4: latency p50 160ms, p95 380ms, cost per 1k tokens $0.35, quality delta -3.7
```
Samir: Quality delta relative to our current 7B baseline?
Lena (ML): Yep — baseline is 7B fp16 at +0.0. 11.5B fp16 slightly better but cost jump is big. Int8 keeps most of gains for ~2x cost reduction vs fp16.
Elaine S: Did we see any failure modes with int8 (hallucinations, answer truncation)?
Lena (ML): Small uptick in factuality errors on long-context QA (~+1.1% error), and occasional tokenization oddities with weird punctuation in code outputs. Not dramatic.
Mike R: For product routing: recommended profile?
Lena (ML): My rec: default route -> 11.5B int8 for standard completions (latency SLO 250ms). Canary/critical flows -> 11.5B fp16 (higher cost). Fallback -> 7B int4 for ultra-cheap non-critical. Add a regression alert on the prompt-set we used (we already flagged two prompts that flip answer).
Samir: What about batching impact — do these numbers assume our 8-request batch at 2048 context?
Lena (ML): Numbers are with dynamic batching tuned for p50. If you push to high throughput (10k qps), int8 throughput improves further and cost per token drops ~12%.
QuantBot: automated-eval: rerank delta: int8 -0.8 BLEU-style, int4 -3.9. hallucination-detector: int8 +1.1%, int4 +4.2%
Elaine S: Sounds reasonable. Any immediate rollout risks?
Lena (ML): Risk list: (1) the 2 prompts that flip answers — add to holdback and run human eval, (2) slightly worse long-context factuality — consider prefix caching to reduce recomputation, (3) tokenization edgecases — add tokenizer fuzz tests. None are showstoppers for a staged rollout.
Mike R: Product ask — can we produce an A/B test plan and estimated unit-econ impact if we shift 30% of traffic to int8?
Lena (ML): Quick calc: current mix (all fp16 7B baseline) cost per 1k tokens $0.60. If we route 30% to 11.5B int8 ($0.58/1k) and 70% remain baseline, blended cost ~ $0.596 (negligible). But quality uplift for customer-facing tasks ~ +0.6 score. If we compare migrating from 7B -> 11.5B int8 across 100% traffic, unit cost jumps but quality improves; we recommend canary then 30% ramp.
Samir: Can you drop the exact formulas in the doc? I can build the dashboard change.
Lena (ML): Formula pasted: blended_cost = sum(traffic_frac_i * cost_i). Example: 0.3*0.58 + 0.7*0.60 = 0.596. Also sensitivity: if latency SLO tightened, int8 p95 might violate at high load -> need autoscale headroom.
Elaine S: OK — I'll write the rollout checklist and add the two prompts to human-eval queue. :thumbsup:
Mike R: great. Lena, can you upload the full eval artifacts to the bench bucket and tag with shelf-testbed/11.5b-int8?
Lena (ML): On it — uploading now. link: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/bench/shelf-testbed/11.5b-int8 (perm: eng-ml read)
QuantBot: ci-note: artifacts uploaded (sha: abc123).
Samir: Awesome. If human eval flags >2 regressions we'll pause ramp. Otherwise go ahead with 5% -> 30% over 48h.
Lena (ML): Plan logged in the runbook. I'll start a canary tomorrow AM.
Mike R: Thanks all.
Elaine S: :rocket:
